patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

Secondary_Symptoms: Difficulty sleeping on the affected side
Difficulty with brushing hair and dressing

patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic left shoulder pain without a history of trauma.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “I’m a 55-year-old woman, and for the past two months I’ve had gradually worsening pain in my left shoulder. It’s worse when I move it to extremes or use it, it disrupts my sleep, and I’m having trouble with daily activities like brushing my hair and getting dressed.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any obvious swelling in my joints, but the pain in my left shoulder is definitely getting worse with movement, and it’s been affecting my sleep and daily activities like brushing my hair and dressing.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere on my body.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, lifting my left arm above my head is very difficult and really brings on the pain, especially at the extremes of motion.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any loss of vision at all—there’s no vision change or anything like that.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had a fever or felt extremely hot, and I haven’t been dizzy or unusually uncomfortable from any illness.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately; the main issue has been the steadily worsening left shoulder pain over the past two months, especially with extreme movement, and it’s been disrupting my sleep and daily activities like brushing my hair and dressing.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t had any chills or felt unusually cold.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breasts that feel fixed or don’t move. My main concern is the steadily worsening pain in my left shoulder, especially with movement to extremes, and it’s been affecting my sleep and daily activities like brushing my hair and dressing.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had pain or discomfort on the side of my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips—my discomfort is mainly focused in my left shoulder.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any calf pain when I walk, and it doesn’t seem to go away with rest because it hasn’t been happening in the first place.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes—moving my left arm up overhead and also across my body is very difficult, and it especially brings on the pain when I get to those extreme positions.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you notice joint pain or stiffness after repeated use, such as after long periods of typing or playing sports?
turns.patient_answer: “I do notice that repeated use of my left shoulder makes the pain worse, especially as I push it to extremes of motion. It also makes it hard to do things like brushing my hair and getting dressed, and it continues to disrupt my sleep.”
